info.title: Omnigraph API
info.description: HTTP API for the Omnigraph graph database

get.summary: List every graph currently registered with this server.
get.description:
Multi-graph mode only. In single mode, the route returns 405 — there's
no registry to enumerate. Cedar-gated by the server-level policy via
the `graph_list` action against `Omnigraph::Server::"root"`.

Order: alphabetical by `graph_id` (server-sorted so clients see
deterministic output across requests).

get.summary: Deliver one logical node or edge Blob cell.
get.description:
Managed content is streamed through the bounded transport. External
descriptors redirect without target-store I/O. Authorization and target
resolution share the exact helper used by `/query`.

This is a distinct handler rather than Axum's automatic GET-to-HEAD
fallback. It never calls `BlobReader::read_range`; Range and If-Range are
deliberately ignored while If-None-Match is still evaluated.

get.description: Returns branch names sorted alphabetically. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.description:
Forks `name` off of `from` (defaults to `main`). The new branch shares
backing dataset data with its parent until it is mutated. Returns 409 if `name`
already exists.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

503.description: An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before retry

post.description:
Merges `source` into `target` (defaults to `main`). Outcome is one of
`already_up_to_date`, `fast_forward`, or `merged`. Returns 409 with the
list of conflicts if the merge cannot be completed; the target is left
unchanged in that case. **Destructive** to `target` on success.

With `delete_branch: true` the source branch is deleted after a successful
merge, under its own `branch_delete` policy check. The merge is durable by
then, so a deletion refusal or failure never fails the request; it is
reported via `branch_deleted: false` + `branch_delete_error`.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

delete.description:
**Irreversible.** Removes the branch pointer; commits remain reachable
only if referenced by another branch. Returns 404 if the branch does not
exist.

get.summary: Poll the change feed of one branch.
get.description:
At-least-once: retrying a cursor may replay the complete next commit, so
consumers apply blocks idempotently by `graph_commit_id` and persist the
terminal cursor together with its blocks. The server holds no consumer
state.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch whose first-parent history is polled. Defaults to `main`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Durable cursor from a prior terminal page. Mutually exclusive with
`start` and `page_token`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Explicit start mode: `now` (default) | `beginning` |
`after:<commit_id>`. Mutually exclusive with `cursor` and `page_token`.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description:
Continuation of one bounded poll (keeps its captured cut). Mutually
exclusive with `cursor` and `start`.

200.description: Change blocks in first-parent order. The durable cursor appears only on a terminal page, advanced only over complete commits; a mid-block page carries only next_page_token

400.description: Invalid start/filter combination, or a rejected cursor or page token

409.description: The feed crossed an unprovable schema boundary; see change_diff_refusal

410.description: Feed gap: required history was reclaimed; reset via the baseline handshake

413.description: Requested limit exceeds the public change ceiling

503.description: Recovery required before changes can be read

post.summary:
Capture a change-feed baseline: one exact entity snapshot plus the cursor
that resumes the feed immediately after it.
post.description:
A baseline is a full data export, so it requires the export action. The
snapshot honors the scope's kind and type dimensions; `op` binds only the
resume cursor's feed scope.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

200.description: NDJSON entity snapshot pinned at one captured commit. Every preceding record is one type-keyed entity record (the load/export NDJSON shape); the FINAL record is the ChangeBaselineRecord envelope — an interrupted stream has no terminal record and therefore no usable cursor. Install the snapshot durably before the cursor.

413.description: Baseline cut or transport capacity exhausted

500.description: Internal failure while capturing the baseline

get.description:
`branch` selects which history to list: a named branch returns the history
reachable from that branch's head (the main commits inherited up to the
fork plus the branch-authored commits); omitting it returns `main`'s
history. There is no cross-branch listing. Ordering is part of the
contract — newest first by (graph-manifest version, created-at, commit id) — and
a future `cursor`/`limit` pagination will be keyset-based on that same
order. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

get.description:
Returns the commit's graph-manifest version, parent commit(s), and creation
metadata. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: commit_id
parameters.description: Commit identifier

get.summary: Entity changes one commit made relative to its first parent.
get.description:
Read-only, in graph vocabulary with exact before/after images. Bounded:
a large commit continues via the opaque `page_token`.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: commit_id
parameters.description: Commit identifier

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque continuation from the preceding page of this response.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum changes per page. Server default applies when absent; above
the public ceiling the request fails with 413.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Repeatable filter: node | edge.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Repeatable filter: accepted-schema type name.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: Repeatable filter: insert | update | delete.

200.description: Entity changes this commit made relative to its first parent, in frozen (kind, type, id, op) order with the cause stated once

400.description: Invalid filter or limit, or a rejected page token

404.description: Commit not found, or the actor cannot read the commit's branch

409.description: Commit cannot be entity-diffed (parentless commit or schema boundary); see change_diff_refusal

410.description: Required retained history is no longer readable; see change_feed_gap and capture a new baseline

413.description: Requested limit exceeds the public change ceiling

503.description: Recovery required before changes can be read

post.summary: Stream the contents of a branch as NDJSON.
post.description:
Emits one JSON object per line (`application/x-ndjson`). Filter with
`type_names` (node/edge type names); an empty list streams the entire branch.
Suitable for large exports — the response is streamed, not buffered.
Read-only.

parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

vocabulary. New integrations should target `POST /load`. Responses
include `Deprecation: true` and `Link: <load>; rel="successor-version"`
headers per RFC 9745 / RFC 8288 so SDKs and proxies can surface the signal.

parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.summary: Compatibility-load NDJSON data through a JSON envelope.
post.description:
`data` is NDJSON with one record per line. `mode` controls behavior on
existing entities: `merge` upserts by id (default), `append` strictly inserts
absent ids, and `overwrite` replaces type data. Branch creation is opt-in by
presence of `from`: with `from` set, a missing `branch` is created from
it; without `from`, `branch` must already exist — a missing branch is a
404, never an implicit fork. **Destructive** when `mode` is `overwrite`
or when the load produces conflicting writes.

The legacy `POST /ingest` route has identical semantics and is kept as a
deprecated alias.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

413.description: Load input or external Blob admission exceeds a bounded per-operation entity or byte ceiling

503.description: An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before retry

post.summary: Load one strict, bounded graph-level NDJSON batch.
post.description:
Bearer authentication runs in middleware. This handler completes both
branch authorization checks before polling the raw body. A successful
response describes logical schema declarations only and is returned after
the ordinary graph commit is visible.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Target branch. Defaults to `main`. Without `from`, it must exist.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Parent branch used to create a missing target branch.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: How existing entities are handled. Defaults to `merge`.

requestBody.description: Strict raw graph-level NDJSON. Each nonblank line is exactly one node envelope {"type":"<Node>","data":{...}} or edge envelope {"edge":"<Edge>","from":"<src-id>","to":"<dst-id>","data":{...}}. `data` defaults to {}; optional `data.id` follows ordinary ID semantics. Duplicate, unknown, reserved physical, and noncanonical supplied node-ID members are refused.

424.description: An allowed external Blob source could not be probed or read

503.description: An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before retry

post.summary: Apply a GQ mutation to a branch (canonical mutation endpoint).
post.description:
Writes to the named `branch` (defaults to `main`). Mutations are atomic
per call and produce a new commit. Returns counts of nodes and edges
affected. **Destructive**: on success the branch is updated; rejected
mutations may still acquire locks briefly. Returns 409 when the prepared
write authority changes before effects.

Conditional callers use `POST /mutate/if-graph-commit`. Keeping that
capability on a distinct path makes rolling upgrades fail closed: an older
server returns 404 instead of ignoring an unknown optional header and
mutating unconditionally.

Pairs with `POST /query` (read-only). The legacy `POST /change` route
has identical semantics and is kept as a deprecated alias.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

424.description: An allowed external Blob source could not be probed or read

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

503.description: An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before retry

post.summary: Apply a mutation only while the branch still has the required graph head.
post.description:
The dedicated path is the rolling-safe capability signal. Clients must not
send this header to `/mutate`: an older server could ignore an unknown
optional header after executing the write.

parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit
parameters.description: Required raw graph-head commit id. The mutation runs only while the branch's effective head still equals it.

get.summary: List the graph's exposed stored queries as a typed tool catalog.
get.description:
Returns every stored query in the `queries:` registry, each
with its MCP tool name, read/mutate flag, description/instruction, and
typed parameters — enough for a client to register them as tools without
fetching `.gq` source. Cluster-served graphs have no per-query expose flag,
so the catalog lists them all. Read-gated; the catalog is graph-wide (branch
independent — `read` is authorized against `main`). **Not** Cedar-filtered
per query yet, so it can list a query whose `invoke_query` the caller
lacks (a known gap until per-query authorization lands).

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

200.description: Stored-query catalog (every stored query, with typed params)

post.summary: Invoke a curated, server-side stored query by name.
post.description:
The query source comes from the graph's `queries:` registry, not the
request body — callers send only runtime inputs (`params`, `branch`,
`snapshot`). Gated by the `invoke_query` Cedar action at the boundary;
a stored *mutation* additionally passes the engine's `change` gate
(double-gated). An actor **without** `invoke_query` cannot tell a denied
query from a missing one — both return the same 404, so the catalog
can't be probed without the grant. Once `invoke_query` is held, the
inner `read`/`change` gate may surface a 403 for an existing query the
actor can't run (the intended double-gate signal).

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Stored query name (the registry key)

200.description: Read envelope (ReadOutput) or mutation envelope (ChangeOutput), serialized untagged

403.description: Forbidden (the inner `change` gate for a stored mutation)

404.description: Unknown stored query, or `invoke_query` denied — indistinguishable to a caller without the grant

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

500.description: Policy evaluation error (a denial is reported as 404, not 500)

503.description: A stored mutation is blocked by a durable recovery intent

post.summary: Execute an inline read query (friendlier-named alternative to `POST /read`).
post.description:
Designed for ad-hoc exploration and AI-agent tool-use: short field
names (`query`, `name`) match the CLI `-e` flag and the GQ `query`
keyword. Mutations (`insert`/`update`/`delete`) are rejected with 400
-- use `POST /mutate` (or its deprecated alias `POST /change`) for
write queries. It shares `POST /read` target semantics (branch xor
snapshot) and the same Cedar action (Read), while its canonical response
additionally carries the pinned graph-commit token.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

400.description: Bad request - also returned when the query body contains mutations; use POST /mutate (or its deprecated alias POST /change) for write queries

409.description: Full-text index requires explicit rebuilding; full_text_index_rebuild_required is not cleared by retrying

post.description:
Execute a GQ read query. Behavior is unchanged from prior releases; the
route is kept indefinitely for byte-stable back-compat. New integrations
should target `POST /query`, which has clean field names (`query` /
`name`) and a 400-on-mutation guard. Responses from this route include
`Deprecation: true` and `Link: <query>; rel="successor-version"`
headers per RFC 9745 / RFC 8288 so SDKs and proxies can surface the
signal.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

200.description: Legacy token-free query results (response includes `Deprecation: true` + `Link: <query>; rel="successor-version"`)

get.description:
Returns the project's schema as a single string in `.pg` source form.
Useful for clients that want to introspect available types and properties
before constructing GQ queries. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.description:
Cluster-backed servers reject this route with `409 Conflict`; operators
must apply schema changes through `omnigraph cluster apply` and restart.

Diffs `schema_source` against the current schema and applies the resulting
migration steps (add/drop type, add/drop property, etc.). **Destructive**:
some steps drop data. Returns the list of steps applied; if `applied` is
false the diff was unsupported and no changes were made.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

409.description: Schema apply is disabled for cluster-backed serving; use `omnigraph cluster apply` and restart

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

get.summary: Read the current snapshot of a branch.
get.description:
Returns the graph-manifest version plus per-dataset metadata (path,
published dataset version, entity count) for every backing dataset on the
branch. Defaults to `main` when `branch` is omitted. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

get.description:
Returns server status and version. Unauthenticated; safe to call from any
caller. Use this to confirm the server is reachable before invoking other
endpoints.

Unauthenticated. Reports whether this replica is serving or draining,
the applied `config_digest` it booted from, the ledger revision and CAS
it read, and the graphs it serves and does not serve. Answers 503 once
shutdown has begun; `/healthz` stays 200 while the process is alive.

BlobEntityKind.description:
Logical graph entity selected by the Blob delivery surface.

This is intentionally graph vocabulary: callers select a node or edge.

BlobRangeOutput.description:
Normalized half-open range details for an unsatisfiable managed Blob read.

HTTP also returns `Content-Range: bytes */N`; these fields let SDKs inspect
the failure without parsing either that header or the human-readable text.

from.description: Parent branch to fork from. Defaults to `main`.

name.description: Name of the new branch. Must not already exist.

branch_delete_error.description:
Why the requested source-branch deletion did not happen. Present iff
`branch_deleted` is `false`.

branch_deleted.description:
Result of the requested post-merge source-branch deletion. Absent when
`delete_branch` was not requested; `true` when the source branch was
deleted; `false` when the deletion was refused or failed (the merge
itself still succeeded — see `branch_delete_error`).

delete_branch.description:
Delete the source branch after a successful merge. The deletion runs
under its own `branch_delete` policy check; a refusal or failure is
reported via `branch_deleted` / `branch_delete_error` on the response
and never fails the already-landed merge.

source.description: Source branch whose commits will be merged.

target.description: Target branch that will receive the merge. Defaults to `main`.

ChangeBaselineOutput.description:
Terminal payload of a baseline stream: the captured snapshot commit and
the cursor that resumes the feed immediately after it.

ChangeBaselineRecord.description:
Wire envelope of the FINAL baseline stream line: `{"baseline": {...}}`,
distinguishable from snapshot records (which carry `type`/`edge` keys).
Emitted exactly once, only after every snapshot record — an interrupted
stream has no terminal record and therefore no usable cursor.

ChangeBaselineRequest.description: Body for the change baseline handshake.

kind.description:
Feed scope the resume cursor is bound to. The snapshot honors `kind`
and `type`; `op` constrains only subsequent polls.

ChangeBlockOutput.description: One commit block inside a feed page.

ChangeCauseOutput.description: The commit cause of one change block, stated once.

authored_at.description:
Authorship time as Unix epoch microseconds — minted before dataset
effects and stable across retries; deliberately not labeled a commit or
publication time.

authored_branch.description: The branch the commit originally landed on (not the requested branch).

ChangeDiffRefusalOutput.description: A well-formed entity-diff request this commit cannot satisfy (HTTP 409).

type_name.description: The graph type at the schema boundary, when the reason names one.

ChangeDiffRefusalReason.description: Why a well-formed entity-diff request was refused (HTTP 409).

ChangeEndpointsOutput.description:
Edge endpoints as graph references. Endpoints belong to each image, so an
endpoint-moving update has distinct before and after endpoints.

ChangeErrorOutput.description:
Error envelope for the read-only change surfaces (`…/changes`,
`…/changes/baseline`, `…/commits/{commit_id}/changes`): a wire-compatible
projection of [`ErrorOutput`] restricted to the graph-vocabulary details
those routes can produce after their error projection. The write-path
conflict shapes (key / published-dataset-version / merge / read-set) are
structurally absent because change routes cannot produce them. Servers
serialize [`ErrorOutput`]; every field a change route can populate appears
here with the same name and meaning, and absent optionals are wire-compatible.

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 409 when a commit entity diff is refused (parentless
commit or an unprovable schema boundary).

Set with HTTP 410 when retained history can no longer reconstruct a
change continuation. Recover via the baseline handshake.

Set with HTTP 503 when the graph has a durable recovery intent that
must be resolved before the requested change read can proceed.

Set when a requested limit exceeds a public ceiling, or a single change
exceeds the poll's own byte ceiling.

ChangeFeedGapOutput.description:
A change continuation can no longer be reconstructed from retained history
(HTTP 410). Recovery is the baseline handshake; retrying the same cursor
cannot succeed. `code` stays unset: [`ErrorCode`] is closed and this
additive detail is the machine-readable discriminator (the same rolling
contract as `external_blob_source`).

caught_up.description:
Present with `cursor` on a terminal page: true when the page reached
its captured head, false when more complete commits already wait.

cursor.description:
Durable caller-owned cursor, advanced only over complete commits and
returned only on a terminal page — an interrupted poll never advances
it.

next_page_token.description: Continue this poll's captured cut. Absent on a terminal page.

ChangeImageOutput.description: One exact logical entity image, decoded with the commit-era schema.

properties.description: Exact logical property values; user-schema keys verbatim.

ChangeOpOutput.description:
Logical operation of one change. Ordering rank is frozen:
insert before update before delete within one entity.

name.description:
Name of the mutation to run when `query` declares multiple.

Accepts the legacy field name `query_name` as a deserialization alias.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the mutation's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ mutation source containing `insert`, `update`, or `delete` statements.
May declare multiple named mutations; pick one with `name`.

Accepts the legacy field name `query_source` as a deserialization alias.

ChangeTypeOutput.description:
Graph-scoped type identity. `id` is opaque: it survives a supported rename
and changes after drop/re-add. It is not a type-name selector or path.

CommitChangesOutput.description: One bounded page of the finite commit entity diff.

next_page_token.description:
Continue THIS bounded response. Absent on the final page. Never a feed
cursor.

created_at.description: Commit creation time as Unix epoch microseconds.

EntityChangeOutput.description:
One entity change. Cause is stated once on the enclosing block, never here.
An insert carries only `after`, an update exact `before` and `after`, a
delete only `before`.

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 416 for a valid but unsatisfiable managed Blob byte range.
`start..end` is half-open and `length` is the selected Blob length.

Set with HTTP 409 when a commit entity diff is refused (parentless
commit or an unprovable schema boundary).

Set with HTTP 410 when retained history can no longer reconstruct a
change continuation. Recover via the baseline handshake.

Set with HTTP 424 when an external Blob URI passed admission policy but
its source could not be probed or read. This optional detail is the
rolling-safe machine-readable discriminator; `code` is omitted because
[`ErrorCode`] is a closed compatibility contract.

Set with HTTP 409 when a selected full-text index requires an explicit
rebuild before search can succeed. Unlike a write-authority conflict,
this condition is not cleared by retrying. This additive discriminator
preserves the closed [`ErrorCode`] contract.

Set when a strict keyed insert found an existing or concurrently
inserted logical id.  The caller may choose a different id; replaying
the same strict operation will not convert it into an upsert.

Set when a mutation's graph-commit precondition failed
(HTTP 412). Like `recovery_required`, the meaning rides this additive
field — `ErrorCode` is a closed rolling wire contract.

Set when the conflict is a publisher CAS rejection. The caller's
pre-write view named the expected published dataset version, but the
graph manifest now publishes the actual version. Refresh and retry.
Set when a prepared write's logical authority changed before effects.

Set when an overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before
retry. Its dataset effects may or may not have started.

Set when the request must be split into smaller graph commits. The
rejected attempt has no durable sidecar and no dataset effect.

type_names.description: Restrict the export to these node/edge type names. Empty exports all types.

ExternalBlobSourceOutput.description:
Structured details for an allowed external Blob source that could not be
probed or read. The top-level `code` remains optional so this additive
detail can roll out without extending the closed [`ErrorCode`] enum.

reason.description:
Source-side failure diagnosis. Clients should branch on the presence of
`external_blob_source`, not parse this human-readable text.

uri.description: Normalized, credential-free URI spelling (or a redacted placeholder).

FullTextIndexRebuildRequiredOutput.description:
A selected full-text index cannot safely serve the current analyzer (HTTP 409).
This is not a retryable write conflict: an operator must rebuild the live
branch's indexes. Historical snapshots stay unchanged; branch old content
and rebuild that branch to search it.

reason.description:
Human-readable diagnosis; branch on the enclosing detail's presence,
not this text, to distinguish the operator-action-required condition.

GraphBatchDeclarationOutput.description:
One logical declaration touched by a graph-batch load.

This deliberately carries the accepted-schema name, not a backing dataset
selector, path, or Lance identity.

GraphBatchLoadOutput.description: Terminal result for the raw graph-level NDJSON load surface.

base_branch.description:
Base branch a fork was requested from, even when the target already
existed. `null` when the request omitted `from`.

edges.description: Logical edge declarations touched by this batch, sorted by name.

nodes.description: Logical node declarations touched by this batch, sorted by name.

GraphInfo.description:
One entry in the response from `GET /graphs`. Cluster operators
consume this list to discover which graphs the server is currently
serving. The shape is intentionally minimal — `graph_id` and `uri`
are the only fields a routing client needs.

GraphListResponse.description:
Response from `GET /graphs`. Lists every graph registered with the
server in alphabetical order by `graph_id` (sorted server-side so
clients get deterministic output across requests).

internal_schema_version.description: The internal-schema (storage-format) version this binary writes and reads.

base_branch.description:
Base branch a fork was requested from (the request's `from`), echoed
even when the branch already existed. `null` when `from` was absent.

edges.description: Logical edge declarations touched by this load, sorted by name.

nodes.description: Logical node declarations touched by this load, sorted by name.

branch.description:
Target branch. Defaults to `main`. Without `from`, the branch must
already exist — a missing branch is a 404, never an implicit fork.

data.description:
NDJSON payload: one record per line, each shaped
`{"type": "<TypeName>", "data": {...}}`.

from.description:
Parent branch used to create `branch` if it does not exist. Branch
creation is opt-in by presence of this field; omit it to require an
existing branch.

oneOf.description: How existing entities are handled. Defaults to `merge`.

InvokeStoredQueryRequest.description:
Body for `POST /queries/{name}` — invokes the server-side stored query
named in the path. The query source and name come from the registry,
never the body; only the runtime inputs are supplied here.

branch.description:
Branch to run against. Defaults to `main`; for a stored mutation the
write targets this branch.

expect_mutation.description:
The kind the caller expects: `Some(false)` for
`omnigraph query <name>`, `Some(true)` for `omnigraph mutate <name>`.
When set and it disagrees with the stored query's actual kind, the
server rejects the call (400) so the verb asserts the kind. `None`
(the default) skips the check — preserving older clients and aliases.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the stored query's declared parameters.

snapshot.description:
Snapshot id to read from (read queries only — rejected for a stored
mutation). Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

InvokeStoredQueryResponse.description:
Response for `POST /queries/{name}`: the read envelope for a stored
read, or the mutation envelope for a stored mutation. Serialized
**untagged**, so the wire shape is exactly [`ReadOutput`] or
[`ChangeOutput`] — classification follows the stored query, not a
wrapper field.

LegacyReadOutput.description:
Indefinitely byte-stable response shape for the deprecated `POST /read`
route. The canonical [`ReadOutput`] may grow additive fields; this legacy
envelope deliberately cannot carry them.

LoadMode.description: Shadow enum for documenting [`LoadMode`] in the OpenAPI schema.

ParamDescriptor.description: One declared parameter of a stored query, projected for the catalog.

oneOf.description:
Element kind when `kind == list` (always a scalar — the grammar
forbids lists of vectors or nested lists).

nullable.description: `false` → the caller must supply it; `true` → optional.

ParamKind.description:
The kind of a stored-query parameter, decomposed so a client (e.g. an
MCP server) can build a typed input schema with a closed `match` and
never re-parse omnigraph's type spelling. `bigint`/`date`/`datetime`/
`blob` are carried as JSON strings on the wire: a 64-bit integer past
2^53 loses precision as a JSON number, and Date/DateTime are ISO
strings, Blob a blob-URI string.

PreconditionFailureOutput.description:
Structured details for a caller write-precondition failure: HTTP 412, a
mutation carried `Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit: <commit_id>`, and the branch
head no longer matches that id. The write had no effect; the caller re-reads
the branch and decides again. `actual` is `None` on a branch with no commits.

PublishedDatasetVersionConflictOutput.description:
Structured details for a publisher-level OCC failure. Surfaces alongside
HTTP 409 when a write was rejected because the caller's pre-write view of
one backing dataset's published version was stale relative to the current
head. The expected/actual fields tell the client which dataset to refresh.

QueriesCatalogOutput.description:
Response for `GET /queries`: every stored query in a graph's
registry, each with typed parameters.

QueryCatalogEntry.description: One entry in the stored-query catalog (`GET /queries`).

mutation.description: `true` for a stored mutation → an MCP read-only hint of `false`.

QueryRequest.description:
Inline read-query request for `POST /query`.

Friendlier-named alternative to [`ReadRequest`] for ad-hoc reads and
AI-agent integration. Mutations are rejected with 400 — use `POST
/mutate` (or its deprecated alias `POST /change`) for write queries.
Field names are deliberately short (`query`, `name`) to match the GQ
keyword and the CLI `-e` flag.

branch.description: Branch to read from. Mutually exclusive with `snapshot`. Defaults to `main`.

name.description:
Name of the query to run when `query` declares multiple. Optional when
only one query is declared.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the query's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ read-query source. May declare one or more named queries; pick one
with `name` when more than one is declared. Mutations
(`insert`/`update`/`delete`) get 400 — use `POST /mutate` (or its
deprecated alias `POST /change`) instead.

snapshot.description: Snapshot id to read from. Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

graph_commit_id.description:
Effective graph head commit id of the exact snapshot this read was
served from. On a fresh named branch this is the inherited source head,
so it is immediately usable as `Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit` (CLI:
`--if-commit`) for the branch's first conditional write. The id and rows
come from one pinned version, so no separate id fetch is needed.

branch.description: Branch to read from. Mutually exclusive with `snapshot`. Defaults to `main`.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the query's declared parameters.

query_name.description:
Name of the query to run when `query_source` declares multiple. Optional
when only one query is declared.

query_source.description:
GQ query source. May declare one or more named queries; pick one with
`query_name` if there is more than one.

snapshot.description: Snapshot id to read from. Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

ReadSetConflictOutput.description:
Structured authority mismatch for a prepared write. Values are
strings because members include optional graph commit ids and future
authority tokens, not only numeric published dataset versions.

ReadinessOutput.description:
The readiness witness of one replica (`GET /readyz`, RFC 0048): whether
it is serving or draining, the applied revision it booted from, and the
graphs it does and does not serve.

booted_serving_digest.description:
The `config_digest` of the applied revision this process booted from.
Fixed for the life of the process: the server never reloads.

quarantined_graphs.description:
Graphs the applied revision names that this process does not serve,
for any reason, sorted.

ready.description: False once shutdown has begun; the response is then 503.

shutdown_grace_seconds.description: The bound on graceful shutdown, after which the process exits 2.

state_cas.description: The ledger CAS (`sha256:<hex>`) the process booted from.

state_revision.description: The ledger revision the process booted from.

ResourceLimitOutput.description:
A write rejected before durable recovery ownership because its bounded
physical plan exceeded an explicit entity, byte, or transaction-chain ceiling.

allow_data_loss.description:
When true, promote every `DropMode::Soft` step in the plan to
`DropMode::Hard`, making the prior property data unreachable
after the apply. Matches the CLI's `--allow-data-loss` flag.
Defaults to `false` (drops remain reversible via time travel).

schema_source.description:
Project schema in `.pg` source form. The diff against the current
schema produces the migration steps that will be applied.

internal_schema_version.description:
The on-disk internal-schema (storage-format) version this graph's branch
is stamped at.
